limitations_and_boundaries: Metabolomic analysis focused primarily on acetaldehyde; comprehensive screening of other aldehydes was not performed.
Systematic assessment of long-term stability, engraftment dynamics, and safety profile of the engineered probiotic in the gut environment remains important for clinical translation.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

missed_core_items.source_excerpt: HFHFD-fed mice treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics exhibited minimal fibrosis, contrasting with severe collagen accumulation in untreated HFHFD mice, with bridging fibrosis (Figures 2A–2C).

missed_core_items.description: The extraction omits the key result that fecal acetaldehyde levels positively correlated with NAS in mice and with FIB-4 index in patients.

research_questions.statement: How does high dietary sugar intake promote progression from MASLD to MASH, and can targeting microbiota-generated acetaldehyde prevent this progression?

provenance.text_excerpt: Acetaldehyde promotes fibrosis through stellate cell activation and MMP7 upregulation

claims.statement: Acetaldehyde promotes hepatic fibrosis by inducing MMP7 expression in hepatic stellate cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: Collectively, these findings provide compelling evidence that the excessive acetaldehyde in MASH is primarily of gut microbial origin, instead of host ethanol metabolism or systemic ethanol load.

claims.statement: Excessive acetaldehyde in MASH is primarily of gut microbial origin, not from host ethanol metabolism or systemic ethanol load.

experiments_or_tasks: Administer low-dose acetaldehyde (50 mg/kg/day) orally to HFD-fed mice for 18 weeks to assess its effect on hepatic inflammation and fibrosis.
Analyze public human liver transcriptomic datasets (GDS4881, GDS4389) for MMP7 levels.
Cell-type mapping analysis to identify HSCs as central mediators.
Demonstrate that excessive acetaldehyde in MASH is primarily of gut microbial origin using ADH activity inhibitor (4-MP) and Aldh2 knockout mice.
Inhibit MMP7 in LX2 cells to confirm its role in fibrogenesis.
Perform HSC-specific Mmp7 knockdown using AAV-shMmp7 in HFHFD-fed mice.
Perform liver-specific Aldh2 knockdown using AAV-shAldh2 in HFHFD-fed mice to assess impact on fibrosis.
RNA-seq on liver tissues from 28-week cohort (control, HFD, HFHFD) and 18-week cohort (HFD ± acetaldehyde) to identify common DEGs.
Treat LX2 cells with low-dose acetaldehyde and measure MMP7 expression via RNA-seq and western blot.

provenance.text_excerpt: Having confirmed its in vitro efficacy, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of L. salivarius and L. salivarius HAM in a mouse model of diet-induced liver disease.

claims.statement: Engineered L. salivarius HAM enhances acetaldehyde clearance and prevents liver fibrosis in preclinical models.

experiments_or_tasks: Assess liver function (ALT, AST), liver enlargement, stiffness, histology (inflammation, fibrosis, NAS), hepatic and fecal acetaldehyde levels, and gene expression.
Engineer L. salivarius to overexpress adhE gene, generating L. salivarius HAM.
Evaluate therapeutic potential in HFHFD-fed mouse model: oral administration of PBS, L. salivarius ATCC, isolated L. salivarius, or L. salivarius HAM every other day for 6 weeks.
Identify L. salivarius as the strain with superior acetaldehyde clearance.
Measure in vitro acetaldehyde clearance of L. salivarius HAM compared to wild-type.
Metagenomic sequencing to assess gut microbial diversity.
Screen probiotics with high acetaldehyde-metabolizing capacity from fecal samples of 51 ALD patients.
Subacute toxicity assessment with high-dose (2×10^10 CFU) probiotic administration.

methods.name: Probiotic screening
methods.protocol_description: Fecal samples from 51 ALD patients with low fibrosis and steatosis scores were used to isolate bacterial clones on selective media. Strains were screened for acetaldehyde degradation activity.

methods.name: Whole-genome sequencing and ANI analysis
methods.protocol_description: WGS and ANI analysis were performed to confirm taxonomic identity of isolated L. salivarius strain.

methods.name: Engineering L. salivarius HAM
methods.protocol_description: The adhE gene was overexpressed in L. salivarius using pMG36e vector.

methods.name: In vitro acetaldehyde clearance assay
methods.protocol_description: Enzymatic assay to measure acetaldehyde degradation activity under ethanol+acetaldehyde and acetaldehyde-only conditions.

methods.name: Mouse model of diet-induced liver disease
methods.protocol_description: Mice were fed HFHFD for 16 weeks, then received oral doses of PBS, L. salivarius ATCC, isolated L. salivarius, or L. salivarius HAM every other day for 6 weeks.

methods.name: Subacute toxicity assessment
methods.protocol_description: Mice were treated with high-dose (2×10^10 CFU) of wild-type or engineered L. salivarius via oral gavage, followed by histological and serum biochemical analysis.

study_units.name: Probiotic screening and engineering
